entries.title: PM Pepe
entries.summary: Message Pepe privately and he answers privately.
entries.details:
Message Pepe privately and he answers privately. He has the **same context he'd have in the room** — who's there, what's been said and micced recently, what's playing, who's on cam — so "what's X on about?" works in a DM.

**He remembers your DMs, privately.** Anything you tell him in a PM is tagged to you and only ever surfaces when he's talking to you in a PM. It never goes into public chat, never becomes room lore, never shows up in anyone else's context, and isn't searchable.

The gate is **who told him**, not who it's about. Tell him your opinion of someone in a DM and he'll remember it for you next time you two talk — and he'll say none of it to them. He won't repeat what anyone else has told him privately either; ask and he'll tell you that straight.

It works one way: a **PM includes everything he knows publicly** — the room, what's been said and micced, who's around — plus what you've told him privately. Public chat gets only the public half.

entries.title: !quote last N | @user N | from <words> to <words>
entries.summary: Turn a bit of the room's chat into a quote post on its pad (bash.org style). Free.
entries.details:
Pepe turns the room's recent lines - chat and 🎙 mic transcripts - into a **quote post** on the room's pad and posts the link. `!quote last 5` takes the last 5 lines (commands left out), `!quote @user 3` that person's last 3 lines with the lines around them, `!quote from <words> to <words>` everything from the line with the first words to the line with the second. Add `| a title` at the end for a title. Up to 20 lines.

Only lines the website already shows can be quoted - never private messages, and people who are `!incognito` or typed `!bridge hide` show as "someone". Anyone quoted can tap **Remove me** on the website to show their lines as "someone". The room must be bridged to its pad (`!bridge on`). Free, a few per half hour. A pad's best quotes: publicaccess.tv/p/<pad>/quotes (with the Quote of the day).

entries.title: !sticker [what you want]
entries.summary: Pepe posts a sticker.
entries.details:
Pepe posts a sticker. `!sticker boring` and he sends a matching one from the catalog he's **learned by watching the room** — he picks up every sticker people use, reads what's on it, and remembers it. `!sticker list` shows how many he knows; `!sticker <set> <id>` forces a specific one. If a send is rejected (a set he can't send) he says so rather than failing silently.

**Reading is automatic:** he quietly understands stickers others post as context — no command needed.

**Reacting on his own** : `!sticker auto on` lets Pepe answer with a fitting sticker when it lands (e.g. a heart when someone says they love him) — opt-in, off by default, and rate-limited. `!sticker reset` wipes what he's learned.

entries.title: -cam [user] — on !ask, !imagine, !roast and !video
entries.summary: Add -cam <user> to make Pepe use that person's live webcam as part of the command.
entries.details:
Add `-cam <user>` to make Pepe use that person's **live webcam** as part of the command.

`!ask what's he drinking -cam tux` — answers from what he can actually see.

`!imagine me as a knight -cam` — uses your cam as the reference image.

`!video make him dance -cam tux` — animates from Tux's cam.

**Or just say it** : `!ask what's on plantbaked's cam?` or `!ask rate my cam` works without the flag, for anyone Pepe has seen in the room.

`!roast tux -cam` — same as **!camroast tux**, kept as an alias.

Bare `-cam` means your own cam. **Several people at once:** repeat the flag or comma-list them — `!ask who looks happier -cam moxier,plantbaked` — and Pepe sees every cam as a separate labelled image in one answer (up to 4). Every `-cam` command costs the command's normal price **plus one vision surcharge per cam** (each is an extra AI call) — the same rule on `!ask`, `!roast` and `!imagine`. Any cam that can't be opened is **refunded**, and if none work you get everything back. Only works in the room Pepe's cam is pointed at.

entries.title: !lotto — PAT Lottery
entries.summary: A Powerball-style weekly lottery.

Pick **4 numbers from 1–30 and a Pepe Ball from 1–10** — `!lotto 3 7 12 25 pb 4` — or let Pepe choose: `!lotto quick`, or `!lotto quick 20` for a stack. Tickets are **PAT 1,000** and there's no limit on how many you hold. The draw is **every Sunday at 9pm ET**, announced in every room and revealed ball by ball on the stream; sales close 5 minutes before. **The jackpot has its own pot**: 40% of every ticket goes into it and it rolls over until someone hits it (then the Federal Reserve restarts it at 1M); the other 60% goes to the casino (the House), which pays the fixed prizes. Capped at 100M. **Prizes:** all 4 + Pepe Ball = the **JACKPOT** (1 in 274,050, split between winners) · 4 = 500k · 3 + PB = 150k · 3 = 15k · 2 + PB = 7.5k · 1 + PB = 3k · Pepe Ball only = 1.5k · 2 = 1k. About **1 in 6 tickets wins something**, and winnings land in your balance automatically. `!lotto` shows the jackpot and next draw, `!lotto tickets` PMs yours, `!lotto results` the last draw, `!lotto odds` the full table.

entries.title: !bingo — PAT Bingo
entries.summary: 75-ball bingo on the stream overlay.
entries.details: 75-ball bingo on the stream overlay. `!bingo start` opens a 60-second lobby; `!bingo buy` gets you a card (**PAT 2,500** each, up to 4 — `!bingo buy 3`), and Pepe PMs you your cards. He then calls a number every few seconds in chat and on the overlay. **You have to call it yourself:** type `!bingo` the moment one of your cards has a complete line — a row, column or diagonal (the centre is free) — and Pepe checks it against the numbers called so far, so you don't need to mark anything. The first line wins **30%** of the prize pool; play continues and the first **full card** wins the rest. Two valid calls on the same ball split the prize. **A wrong call costs PAT 1,000** (it goes into the pot) and benches you for 60 seconds. `!bingo card` re-sends your cards with the called numbers crossed out (XX). 10% of card sales goes to the casino. If nobody calls a prize before all 75 balls are out, it **rolls over** into the next game. Needs at least 2 players; if Pepe restarts mid-game, every card is refunded.

entries.title: !challenge — mic challenges
entries.summary: A room's owner or an admin starts a mic performance; Pepe's AI judges score it out of 10, and good scores win PAT from that room's vault.
entries.details: Only the room's **owner** or a Pepe **admin** can start one. `!challenge sing @bob` counts Bob in: he grabs the mic within 60 s and the judges (an audio AI) score the performance out of 10 with a one-liner. `!challenge open sing 2m` opens a round anyone in the room can enter once with `!sing`. `!challenge sing @a @b 10k` is a head-to-head: both must `!accept` within 60 s, both stakes are held, both perform in turn and the higher score takes the pot minus 5% (half to Fort Knox, half to the room's vault). Ties, no-shows, cancels and judge failures refund the stakes. **Prizes** for solo and open-round goes come from **this room's vault escrow** on publicaccess.tv (the room half of boosts, slot fees and pad gifts): score × 500 PAT from 5/10 (laugh and fart 300), up to 5,000, and a room pays at most 5% of its vault (max 25,000) a day. An empty vault means you play for glory: the score still counts on `!challenge top`. No prize when you start your own challenge or perform in your own room. Recordings, music and TTS are disqualified. Clips are judged in memory and never stored; incognito users can't perform. `!challenge vault` shows this room's prize budget. Admins: `!challenge on|off`, `!challenge status`, `!challenge set <key> <value>`, `!challenge set pay <category> <per point> [min score] [max]`; owners can switch it on or off for their own room.

entries.title: Where drops come from
entries.summary: Some gear can't be bought: it drops when you win something, and Pepe announces it in the room.
entries.details:
Some gear can't be bought: it **drops** when you win something, and Pepe announces it in the room. Rarer items drop less often. Chances per winner:

• **Vault cracked** (casino / bank heist): 25% for each robber. **Arena champion**: 10%. **Bingo**: full card 10%, line 5%. **Paid-out bounty** (10,000+ pot): 15% each hunter, 5% the creator, with bounty-only gear.

• **Everyday wins** (low on purpose, so a drop still means something): convoy taken 5% · duel or brawl won 3% (stake 10,000+) · vault door reached but it held 2% · lotto prize 2% (once per draw) · blackjack natural up to 2% (bet 2,500+; the full 2% at the 10,000 max bet) · hold'em showdown pot 1.5% (pot 20,000+) · clean store getaway 1% · **wheel spin 0.05%** (1 in 2,000).

• **Jackpots**: hitting the lotto jackpot always drops a rare-or-better item; the wheel's jackpot slice has a 25% chance of one.

• Everyday wins give at most **3 drops per 24 hours** per player. Duels and brawls only count against a real opponent (not yourself or your alt, both level 2+), and only the first 3 wins between the same two players each day can drop. Nothing drops until the win has actually been paid.

Bet with `!pool M5 yes 5k` (min 500, as often as you like). When the judge settles it (`!pool settle M5 yes`), the winners split the losing side's pot in proportion to their stakes, after **5% of the losing pot** goes to the casino — so a correct bet never pays back less than you put in. Nobody backed the winner, or it's voided, or the judge never calls it within 7 days: everyone is refunded. `!pools` lists the open ones; they're on [publicaccess.tv/wagers](https://publicaccess.tv/wagers).

entries.title: judge @pepe — Pepe as the judge
entries.summary: Name Pepe as the judge of a market, pool or wager (judge @pepe) and he decides it himself: when trading closes (or every few hours on a wager) he searches the web and, if he's confident,…
entries.details: Name Pepe as the judge of a market, pool or wager (`judge @pepe`) and he decides it himself: when trading closes (or every few hours on a wager) he searches the web and, if he's confident, **proposes** a result with one line of reasoning. It pays out after a **dispute window** (default 1 hour). Anyone with PAT in it can object — `!market dispute M3 why`, `!pool dispute M5 why`, `!wager dispute W3 why` — and enough disputes (one is enough on a wager) send it to an admin. entries.title: !market new [question] judge @someone
entries.summary: Open a prediction market anyone can trade — !market new Will Samira come back this week?
entries.details: Open a **prediction market** anyone can trade — `!market new Will Samira come back this week? judge @carol closes 2d`. Yes/no by default, or give 2–6 answers with `options red/blue/green`. Markets trade **shares**, like Polymarket: each answer has a price between 0 and 1 PAT (the crowd's odds), and every share of the winning answer pays **1 PAT**. Buy with `!market M3 yes 5k` (spend 5k PAT, min 500) — buying pushes the price up, selling pushes it down. Sell any time while trading is open with `!market sell M3 yes 300` or `all`, so you can lock in a profit (or cut a loss) before the result. `!market mine` shows your positions with your entry price, today's price and profit/loss; `!market M3` the prices, `!market list` the open ones. 2% fee on every buy and sell. Trading closes at the set time (default 1 day, max 30); the judge — who can't trade — calls it with `!market settle M3 yes`, or `!market settle M3 void <reason>`. **On a void, trading fees are not refunded** (they were taken when you traded): the Federal Reserve takes back its seed first, then holders split what's left in the market, up to what they put in — so if others sold at a profit before the void, holders get back less. Betting pools and wagers are different: a void there refunds every stake in full, fees included. All of it, judging included, works on [publicaccess.tv/markets](https://publicaccess.tv/markets) with a price chart. The Federal Reserve seeds each market's liquidity and gets back whatever's left over. Start one from the site too. For the old simple pool model, see `!pool`.

entries.summary: The treasury is a shared pot you draw from, not a payroll.
entries.details:
The treasury is a **shared pot you draw from**, not a payroll. There's no daily wage any more — income stays banked and each member takes what they need up to **their rank's daily allowance**: owner unlimited, officer 250,000, member 100,000, recruit 25,000. Allowances are **per person**, so one officer emptying theirs no longer locks out the rest of the crew, and they reset on the daily tick.

`!gang limits` shows the current allowances; the boss sets them with `!gang limits <owner|officer|member|recruit> <amount>` (0 = unlimited). Withdrawals pay a **5% laundering cut** to Canary Wharf on the way out.

entries.title: !gangs reset
entries.summary: The start-over button.
entries.details: The start-over button. Wipes **every** gang — members, treasuries, rep, Turf Score — and clears the whole map, banks and stakes included. Nothing is refunded and there's no undo, so it asks for `!gangs reset confirm`. Distinct from a season ending, which keeps rep and hands stakes back.

entries.title: !turf season · !claim
entries.summary: Turf Score is the season standing, separate from gang rep.
entries.details:
**Turf Score** is the season standing, separate from gang rep. It builds every day you hold a borough — outer 1, mid 2, centre 4 per day (×100) — so a season is won by holding ground over time, not by sweeping the map on the last day. Holding at the final whistle adds up to +25%. `!turf season` shows the table, the day, and the prize pot.

It's also the **invasion gate**: 500 to move on a mid borough, 2,000 for Mayfair. Earned this season, so an old gang doesn't start with the map unlocked.

**Claiming is a crew event.** `!claim <borough>` musters for 45s — crewmates `!join` for 5,000 PAT each — then the whole crew rolls against whoever's already there. 8 rounds outer, 9 mid, 10 centre, 2 strikes each, and numbers genuinely tell (a crew bonus applies from 3 up). Geared success runs about **24% solo · 68% at three · 89% at five** on an outer borough, **39%** at five for a mid one and **17%** for Mayfair — so the crown needs a real gang. **The stake is only paid if you take it**: a failed run costs the buy-ins, never the deposit.

**Season end** (30 days, or `!turf end`): the top score takes the pot — everything the streets banked, matched by the Reserve. Business banks go to the Federal Reserve to seed next season's heists, and **every stake is refunded** — holding turf is never a losing move. Ownership, banks and Turf Score reset; gang rep is permanent and carries over.

entries.title: !heist convoy · !defend · !turf cargo
entries.summary: Every business queues its takings as cargo instead of banking them on the spot.
entries.details:
Every business queues its takings as **cargo** instead of banking them on the spot. Every so often an **armored convoy** leaves carrying the lot — announced in the room, naming the business and the haul — and for **15 minutes** it's on the road and takeable.

**Rivals only:** `!heist convoy` intercepts it. You can't rob your own gang's money. The prize is the cargo itself — every round's loot comes out of it, and survivors split whatever's left; no vault, no door — and the owners never see a penny of what's taken.

**Owners:** `!defend` to ride shotgun. Each guard raises every DC on that run, so a well-escorted convoy is a genuinely bad idea to hit.

If nobody takes it (or the crew gets pinched), what's left of the cargo banks as normal. `!turf cargo` shows what's on the road now, or what's building up if nothing has left yet. This is the valve that keeps PAT moving — what the room spends becomes what the room can steal.

entries.title: !heist [job]
entries.summary: Rob a target, D&D-style — a multi-round survival gauntlet with your !sheet stats, gear, and gang.
entries.details:
Rob a target, D&D-style — a multi-round survival gauntlet with your `!sheet` stats, gear, and gang. Each round everyone rolls 1d20 + a random stat's modifier vs a rising difficulty (plus crew/flawless/gang bonuses). Survive to bank loot, `!bail` to cash out, get pinched and your loot is split among the survivors.
**The vault door:** the casino and bank jobs end at **one shared roll for the whole crew**, made by whoever's best placed for the stat it tests. Open it and the crew splits a slice of the vault — usually a few percent, occasionally a huge haul (up to 40% of the vault, very rarely). Fail it and **everyone at the door loses the loot they were holding** (it stays in the vault) — unless a ⚖️ Good Lawyer saves half. So the last `!bail` window, right before the door, is the big decision: walk away with your loot, or risk it for the vault.
**Odds:** the door is hard on purpose — even a perfect sheet with a full kit opens the casino door only about a third of the time solo, and the Federal Reserve's under 1 in 10; an ordinary sheet still has a real long shot. The bank pays **4× more loot per round** than the casino to make up for it.
**Jobs** (**!heist <job>**, or **!heist list**): 🏪 **store** — small, quick, always open; 🎰 **casino** — 5,000 to join, 9 rounds + the door (needs a 100k+ jackpot); 🚚 **convoy** — rob a gang's cargo run (needs a casino job first; it pays out of the cargo itself); 🏛️ **bank** — 20,000 to join, 11 rounds + the door, the legendary Federal Reserve (needs 📐 Blueprints and a casino job, 500k+ vault). Money jobs are paced by your **own heat** — everyone in the crew takes it, not just the starter — plus a **cooldown per job type** (store 30m, casino 2h, bank 8h) that now survives Pepe restarting. Round loot and the vault slice both scale with the vault, so a fat vault is worth more to everyone. Deep runs can drop rare scores: 📐 Blueprints (unlocks the bank), 🎲 **Loaded Dice** (`!reroll` a stat), 💍 **Kingpin's Ring** (`!ring` +1 a stat), 📈 **The Fence** (+10% payouts), and 🧠 **Mastermind** (advantage on your two best stats). Gear up with `!shop`. See **/heist** for the guide.
**Your loot is real:** what you bank each round is set aside from the vault as you win it, so you always walk out with it. If the vault can't cover a round, Pepe says so — nat 20s get paid first and the rest split what's left.
**Other rooms:** you can `!join` a heist from any room, but the rounds — and `!bail` — only work in the room it's running in.

**Sound is on by default** — the room's audio is recorded into the clip. Two things have to be true, or it records silently and says which failed: the room must be the one Pepe is listening to (see `!audioroom` — the loopback carries one room at a time), and **someone must be on the mic**. `-na` (or `-mute`) records video only; `-ao` records **sound only** — an audio clip of whoever's on the mic, with its own player page.

Clips are downscaled and compressed to stay postable; if someone's cam is too busy to fit even at the smallest setting, Pepe says so and refunds rather than posting a broken link. Ships **switched off** per room like `!snap`.

entries.title: !dj on|off
entries.summary: Put Pepe on the decks — he auto-DJs, generating an eclectic set on the fly: crowd-pleasers, deep cuts, every era and genre, no repeats.
entries.details: Put Pepe on the decks — he **auto-DJs**, generating an eclectic set on the fly: crowd-pleasers, deep cuts, every era and genre, no repeats. He **reads the room** — the songs you `!queue` become cues for what he lines up next. He'll even **drop a spoken DJ line over the intro** of some tracks (ducking the music under his voice) — toggle with **!dj talk on/off** (**per room** — add **-all** or **-global** to widen it; **!dj talk chance <0-100>** sets how often). The DJ only speaks up in rooms actually hearing the set — the ones with **!mic music on** — and holds the drop entirely if any of them has DJ talk switched off, since the mic carries one stream to all of them. **!dj next** cues one now, **!dj genre <g>** nudges the vibe, **!dj min <1-5>** sets how many picks stay queued ahead, **!dj status** shows what's going on. **!dj clear** resets the session for a fresh direction: the vibe, his cues and lined-up picks, and everything waiting in the queue (his picks and listeners' requests — paid requests are refunded; Spotify can't delete from its queue, so those tracks are skipped silently when they come up). The current song plays out and the DJ stays on, waiting for a new `!dj vibe` (up to 3 minutes) before he lines anything else up. **Anyone can steer him:** `!dj vibe <what you want>` (e.g. `!dj vibe 90s hip hop`) — or just say it: "pepe play some chill stuff". He leans the set that way for the next ~45 minutes. He also builds on what's actually in the queue right now, so his picks flow on from your requests instead of duplicating them. **Patter mode (one voice on the mic):** while he DJs a room with DJ talk on, everything he'd otherwise say on the mic by himself — welcome-backs for people who join, chatty mic-ups, conversation starters and shout-outs — goes into one short spoken link between songs (over the next intro, music ducked), built from what happened during the song; five people joining is one "welcome in…", not five clips. Questions to him still get a text reply right away. When nothing happened he may open a topic the room is into (or a light headline). Admins tune it with `!dj patter on|off · every <n> · words <n> · joins|starters|chatty on|off · budget <n>`. **Shout-outs:** `!dj shoutout <name> [message] [-d]` (or `!shoutout`) — the DJ names them in his next link; `-d` dedicates the next song. 2,500 PAT, held when you ask and only taken when he says it (refunded if he hasn't within 30 minutes; `!dj shoutout cancel` to undo) — it's split like other paid room commands: by default 20% to Soho's nightclub, 10% to the room's owner and the rest to the Federal Reserve. One every 15 minutes per person; keep it friendly — no links, and people who are incognito can't be named.

entries.title: !mic grab · force · lock · drop · slots
entries.summary: Pepe's own mic control.
entries.details:
Pepe's own mic control. **grab/hold** takes & holds a mic (re-grabs when a slot frees); **force** seizes a slot even when the mic's full; **lock self,alice,…** restricts the mic to named users (everyone else is blocked) and **unlock** lifts it; **drop** lets go; **slots <n>** sets the room's mic-slot limit.
**Per room:** every room has its own mic button, so holding, hold-mode and force-mode all belong to one room — Pepe can be holding the mic for music in one room while free in another, and stepping into a room to speak one line no longer makes him keep its mic. `!mic drop` lets go of the room you're in (and says where else he's still holding); `!mic drop all` lets go **everywhere**. `!mic status` lists the other rooms he's holding in.
**Scope of a settings command:** `!mic music off`, `!mic tts voice X`, `!mic alerts`, `!mic slots`, `!mic tts on|off|chatty|caption` all change **the room you typed them in** (like `!redlist`). Add `-global` to change the default that rooms without their own setting follow — rooms that do override it are unaffected, and Pepe says so. Add `-all` to change the default and clear every room's override, so every room really gets it.
**Random voice:** set any voice to `random` — `!mic tts voice random`, `!say … -v random`, or the room/alert voice in the panel — and Pepe picks a different one every line. It only ever picks voices that are free for whoever asked, so it can never bill you for a premium voice you didn't choose (admins, who use every voice free, get the full range).
**Per-room settings:** each room can also have its own default voice, chatty-voice frequency, caption/alert switches, jukebox-on-mic setting and mic-slot limit — set them in the admin panel with that room selected. Chat commands like `!mic tts voice` set the global default that rooms without an override follow. The VoiceBox engine, model size and audio device stay global, since there's only one of each.

entries.title: !mic reset
entries.summary: Recovery tool.
entries.details: **Recovery tool.** Makes Pepe forget what he thinks he's holding, in every room — and deliberately **clicks nothing**, so it can't make the client worse. Use it when a room is stuck showing held that `!mic drop` won't clear: dropping a mic that isn't really on would turn it on, so once his belief and the client disagree there's otherwise no way back. Afterwards check the client and use **!mic grab** / **!mic drop** to line them up. (Aliases: **!mic resync**, **!mic forget**.)

entries.summary: status shows everything at once — hold mode, whether the audio pipeline is armed, whether Pepe holds a slot, who else is on the mic, any lock or force-block, and the output device.
entries.details: **status** shows everything at once — hold mode, whether the audio pipeline is armed, whether Pepe holds a slot, who else is on the mic, any lock or force-block, and the output device. **device <name>** sets that output device by substring (e.g. `!mic device CABLE Input`); with no name it just tells you the current one. **test** plays a tone to it, grabbing the mic if needed — the quickest way to check the audio path end to end.

entries.title: !mic force audio on|off
entries.summary: Lets Pepe interrupt a full mic to play a clip — a !say, an alert sting, or a chatty mic-up.
entries.details: Lets Pepe **interrupt a full mic to play a clip** — a `!say`, an alert sting, or a chatty mic-up. When it's on and every slot is taken, he bumps whoever's on, plays the clip, then **drops and unblocks them straight away**. He does not keep the mic, which is what makes this different from plain **!mic force** (that seizes a slot and holds it). Off (the default) he just waits for a slot to free up, and a clip is only dropped if the mic stays full for the whole wait. Handy in a busy room where Pepe would otherwise never get a word in; rude if you leave it on during a serious conversation.

entries.summary: How big moments — a heist forming, a turf invasion, the jackpot cracking, a big win — reach each room.
entries.details:
How big moments — a **heist** forming, a **turf invasion**, the **jackpot** cracking, a **big win** — reach each room. An alert is an event, not a sound: it can arrive by any combination of **three channels**, each switched separately.

**Channels (per room):** `!alerts sound on|off` a sting through the mic · `!alerts tts on|off` Pepe says it out loud · `!alerts text on|off` a line in chat. `!alerts on|off` is the master switch — off and this room gets nothing at all. Like every settings command these change **the room you typed them in**; add `-global` or `-all` to widen.

**Scope (per event, global):** `!alerts heist room` keeps a heist alert in the room it started in. `!alerts heist global` also tells every other room where it's kicking off, by tab name — "a heist is forming in Pepe's Pad". A room with alerts switched off stays quiet either way, so one room can opt out of the noise entirely.

**Voice:** `!alerts voice <name>` gives spoken alerts their own voice in this room, so an alert cuts through instead of sounding like everything else Pepe says. `!alerts voice random` re-rolls one each time, `!alerts voice default` goes back to the room's usual voice. Per room, like the channels.

**Force the mic:** `!alerts jackpot force on` lets that alert **bump whoever is on the mic** so the sting or spoken line actually gets heard, rather than queueing and being dropped if no slot frees up. It cuts someone off mid-sentence, so it's set per event and off by default — worth it for the jackpot, rarely for anything else. Text alerts never need a mic slot and are unaffected.

**Notes:** spoken alerts need TTS on in that room — if it's off they simply don't play there, whatever this is set to. The text channel doesn't repeat itself in the room the event happened in (that room already posts its own announcement); it writes the "it's happening over there" line into the other rooms. `!alerts test <type>` fires one to check your setup, and `!alerts` on its own shows where everything stands. All of it is in the admin panel too.

entries.title: !promo [on|off|now|list] · every · cap · msgs · vary · skip
entries.summary: House ads in chat.
entries.details:
**House ads in chat.** Pepe now and then posts a short line advertising his own games and features (a free `!sponsor` for the house). Off by default. `!promo on|off` switches it for the room you type it in; add `-global` for rooms without their own setting, or `-all` for every room. `!promo` alone shows the status here: on or off, today's count, when the last ad went out and what it's waiting for.

It stays quiet by design: one ad slot per room, **shared with sponsors** (paid sponsors always go first), only while the room is actually talking, never during a game, heist, casino table or lotto draw, never with two or more people on the mic, and the same ad never twice in a room within 24 h.

Settings (all rooms): `!promo every <15-720>` minutes between ads (default 50) · `!promo cap <0-24>` house ads per room per day (default 4) · `!promo msgs <n>` chat lines needed since the last ad (default 15) · `!promo vary on|off` lets the AI reword a line (it keeps every !command and link). `!promo list` shows the ads; `!promo skip <id>` / `unskip <id>` mutes one. `!promo now` tries one here immediately (still skips anything not allowed right now, and says why). Example: `!promo on` then `!promo every 90`. Not the same as `!pepefeed`, which is Pepe on the website feed.

entries.details: **Chatty depth** (per room, default normal): after Pepe answers you, he stays in the conversation for a bit — your next lines that look meant for him get answered without saying "pepe" (short = 3 follow-ups, normal = 6, long = 12; it ends after 1/2/5 quiet minutes, when you say bye/stop, or when the follow-ups run out — saying his name again refreshes them). Lines aimed at someone else (@bob…, bob, …), a bare "lol", or a room that's moved on don't count. Long conversations are summarized in the background so he keeps the thread. `cap` = follow-ups per hour in the room; `memory` = how much of the model's context a conversation fills before it's summarized; `end` stops the conversations in the room. Turns itself down when the daily AI budget runs low.

entries.title: How multiple rooms work
entries.summary: Pepe can sit in several Camfrog rooms at once, and each one is its own place.
entries.details:
Pepe can sit in several Camfrog rooms at once, and each one is its own place.

**People carry over, rooms don't.** What he knows about you follows you between rooms (and he'll say where he heard it — "you mentioned that in the other room"); a room's own lore, chat log and transcripts stay in that room.

**Chat & transcripts are per room.** Anything that quotes history — `!ask`, `!roast`, `!chart`, chatty replies, DJ patter — only draws on the room you're in. So do `!log`, `!replay`, `!search`, `!mictop`, `!micstats` and `!modlog`. Add `-all` to any of those to search or total across every room instead.

**Settings are per room.** Games, chatty, cams and the rest can be switched on in one room and off in another from the admin panel's room selector — only the AI model/API settings are shared.

**Telegram** has its own scope: `/room <name>` focuses a chat on one room, `/room all` widens it. Keyword alerts always cover every room and say which one they came from.

**Voice and cams live in one room at a time** — whichever `!audioroom` / `!activeroom` point at. Mic and cam commands are refused elsewhere with a note saying which room owns them.

entries.title: !audioroom [room] · all
entries.summary: When Pepe is in more than one room, set which room's audio is live.
entries.details:
When Pepe is in more than one room, set which room's **audio** is live. Loopback captures a single audio stream, so only the chosen room's mic-ups get recorded/transcribed — the others are skipped to avoid misattributing what was said. `!audioroom` alone shows the current room and the rooms seen; `!audioroom all` (or `off`) records every room. (Alias: `!microom`.)
**Automatic switching:** once the speaker control is recorded with `!audiobtn`, this actually **moves the audio in the client** — mutes the room that currently has it, switches to the target's tab, then unmutes that one, all in the background with no focus stolen. If any step fails the previous room is unmuted again and the setting is left alone, so you never end up with two rooms feeding one stream, or none. Add `-noswitch` to record the setting **without** touching the client — for when the audio is already where you want it and only the bot's idea of it was wrong. (Also `-nomove` / `-setonly`.)

entries.title: !activeroom [room] [force] · auto
entries.summary: When Pepe is in more than one room, set which room's window is targeted by window-driven actions — his own mic button, the participant-list read, and cam opening.
entries.details:
When Pepe is in more than one room, set which room's **window** is targeted by window-driven actions — his own mic button, the participant-list read, and cam opening. **It's also the main-stage room:** the stream shows Pepe's room window, so pinning a room clicks its tab, the publicaccess.tv homepage shows that room as On stage, and its live room page plays the stream above the chat. Only rooms Pepe is in; it waits while a game is running (add `force` to move it anyway); Pepe's mic and music don't block it. Site admins can do the same from the homepage stage. `!activeroom` alone shows the setting; `!activeroom auto` follows whichever tab is open. `!activeroom <tab label>=<room>` tells Pepe which tab belongs to which room when the two are named differently. (Alias: `!winroom`.)

**Auto-switch:** with Auto-switch room tab on in the admin panel, Pepe changes tabs himself instead of refusing — a window-driven command just runs in the room it was typed in. Spoken audio (`!say`, `-mic` replies, sponsor reads) **queues**: the tab is switched immediately before each clip takes the mic, so several people speaking from different rooms play one after another in the right rooms rather than fighting over the tab. Pinning a room with `!activeroom` disables auto-switching.

entries.details: Reads every room's speaker button and reports which rooms are live, muted, or unknown — and refreshes the mute column in the admin panel's status card. On demand only: reading a room's state means switching to its tab, so it is never polled. Rooms show as unknown until Pepe has had reason to look at them; any `!audioroom` move visits them all and fills the picture in. (Alias: `!mutestatus`.)

entries.summary: Mutes or unmutes one room's audio in the client without changing the !audioroom setting — the repair tool for when the two drift apart.
entries.details: Mutes or unmutes **one room's audio in the client** without changing the `!audioroom` setting — the repair tool for when the two drift apart. Switches to the room first (a speaker button only exists while its room is on screen), then clicks. If the button reports its state on your build these are **idempotent** (a second `!mute` does nothing); if it doesn't, they act as a plain toggle and say so rather than claiming a state they can't see. (Alias: `!roomaudio`.)

entries.title: !audiobtn [id]
entries.summary: Records which control mutes/unmutes a room's audio.
entries.details: Records which control mutes/unmutes a room's audio. Once set, **!audioroom <room>** moves the audio itself — mutes the old room, switches tab, unmutes the new one — with no clicking and without Camfrog taking focus. Without an argument it shows the current setting. Stored per install, since the id can differ between Camfrog builds. With no argument it reports the id and whether **state detection** is calibrated. Pepe works out which button reading means "muted" by comparing every open room — the odd one out is the live one — which is what makes `!mute`/`!unmute` idempotent rather than blind toggles. `!audiobtn recal` re-learns it if it ever gets it wrong; it needs at least two rooms open with exactly one unmuted.

entries.title: !model
entries.summary: Tiered AI model control with per-function overrides.
entries.details:
Tiered AI model control with per-function overrides.


**Tiers:** **primary** (ask/roast/chatty) | **secondary** (charts/polls/prompts) | **background** (memory/trivia/summaries)

**Functions:** ask, roast, chatty, chart, imagine, poll, trivia, memory, summary


**Presets:**

`!model preset quality` — Opus / Sonnet / Haiku

`!model preset max` — Opus / Opus / Opus

`!model preset balanced` — Sonnet / Haiku / Haiku

`!model preset budget` — Sonnet / Haiku / Local

`!model preset local` — everything local Ollama

`!model preset off` — disable all AI (tools still work)


**Tier control:**

`!model all [model]` — set all tiers

`!model primary opus` — set a specific tier


**Per-function override:**

`!model ask opus` — override just !ask to use Opus

`!model chatty local` — override chatty to use local

`!model roast sonnet` — override roasts to use Sonnet

`!model ask reset` — remove override, fall back to tier

`!model reset overrides` — clear all overrides


**Info:**

`!model status` — show tiers + active overrides

`!model list` — list models, presets, and functions


**Intelligent Router:**

`!model preset intelligent` — dynamic model selection based on complexity, budget, and user feedback

`!model mode smart` — LLM-classified routing (uses local gemma3:4b to classify complexity, ~2s). Routes: simple→Haiku, moderate→Sonnet, complex→Opus

`!model mode fast` — rule-based routing (instant, no LLM). Routes: simple→Haiku, moderate→Haiku, complex→Sonnet

The router adapts over time — if users react negatively to a cheaper model's responses, it auto-upgrades. If a model consistently gets positive feedback, it may downgrade to save cost.


**Budget Control:**

`!model budget [amount]` — set daily budget (e.g. `!model budget 5` for $5/day)

`!model budget` — show current spend + remaining

`!model costs` — detailed cost breakdown by model and function

`!model feedback` — show quality scores per model based on user reactions


Models: opus, sonnet, haiku, local, intelligent, off. Auto-falls back to local when API credits run out. Persists between restarts.

Useful for testing a rate change without waiting a day. Runs on its own thread, so the bot stays responsive.

entries.title: !turf reset
entries.summary: Wipes turf ownership back to a blank map and refunds each held borough's stake to its owner's treasury.
entries.details: Wipes turf ownership back to a blank map and refunds each held borough's stake to its owner's treasury. Gangs, members and treasuries survive. Lighter than `!gangs reset` — this clears the board, not the players.

entries.title: !gangs reset
entries.summary: The start-over button.
entries.details: The start-over button. Dissolves **every** gang — members, treasuries, **rep**, Turf Score — and clears the whole map including banks and stakes. Nothing is refunded and there is no undo, so it asks first: `!gangs reset confirm` to go through with it. Distinct from a season ending, which keeps rep and hands stakes back.

entries.title: !vault mint [vault] [amount] · !reserve mint [amount]
entries.summary: Prints PAT straight into either vault.
entries.details:
**Prints PAT straight into either vault.** `!vault mint jackpot|reserve <amount>` — the casino jackpot goes through the backend (it's the same pot the site and Discord see), the Reserve is the bot's own. Aliases work: `casino`/`wheel`/`spin` for the jackpot, `fed`/`bank` for the Reserve. Amounts take `k` and `m` suffixes, so `!vault mint casino 500k` is fine.
This is the only lever in the game that creates PAT rather than moving it, so it's admin-only and **announced in every room** whichever pool it lands in. Use it to seed a vault early in a season, before sink inflow has built it into a target worth robbing. `!reserve mint <amount>` still works as the Reserve shortcut.

`!reserve auto on|off` has the daily tick top the Reserve back up to a floor automatically (**off by default**), and `!reserve floor <amount>` sets that floor. Plain `!reserve` is public and just shows the balance.

entries.title: !turf sinks · !turf cargo
entries.summary: The economy's dashboard.
entries.details: The economy's dashboard. `!turf sinks` shows last tick's captured volume per business and — importantly — how much went **over the sink cap and spilled to the heist vaults**. If one business is swallowing everything, that's where you'll see it. `!turf cargo` shows what's on the road right now or what's queueing for the next convoy.

entries.title: !gang limits [rank] [amount]
entries.summary: Daily treasury withdrawal allowance per rank — owner / officer / member / recruit, set by the gang boss (or an admin).
entries.details: Daily treasury withdrawal allowance per rank — **owner / officer / member / recruit**, set by the gang boss (or an admin). `0 = unlimited`. Anyone can run `!gang limits` to see the current values. This replaced the old flat daily wage: income now stays in the treasury and members draw what they need, so the active get paid and the inactive don't.

entries.title: !alerts
entries.summary: Which big moments reach which rooms, and how.
entries.details: Which big moments reach which rooms, and how. Channels are per room — `!alerts sound|tts|text on|off`, plus `!alerts on|off` as this room's master switch. Scope is per event and global: `!alerts heist room|global`. `!alerts <type> force on|off` lets an alert bump someone off the mic to be heard, and `!alerts voice <name>` gives spoken alerts their own voice. `!alerts test <type>` fires one to check the setup.

entries.title: Economy tuning — admin panel
entries.summary: Every rake, tap and split in the game is editable in the Sink Rates card without touching code: the arena/fight and hold'em rake rates, the tip tap, the treasury-withdrawal laundering…
entries.details: Every rake, tap and split in the game is editable in the **Sink Rates** card without touching code: the arena/fight and hold'em rake rates, the tip tap, the treasury-withdrawal laundering cut, the **sink cap** (the single biggest lever on how much PAT reaches the heist vaults), bank payout and cap multipliers, the mint rate, the season-pot share, and how much incoming vault PAT goes to the Reserve (the rest goes to the casino jackpot). **PAT Routing** decides where the PAT goes for everything Pepe charges — commands, music, voices, heist gear, blackjack losses, rake, lotto, bingo, wager and market fees, fines, loan interest: up to three destinations per row (the casino jackpot, the Reserve, a turf business, or - for room-specific spending like commands, song requests, voices and shout-outs - the **room's owner**, 10% by default, paid weekly from the Reserve; a room with no owner leaves it in the Reserve) as a % of the price, and whatever isn't routed goes to the Federal Reserve — PAT is never burned. The same table says which vault **pays** each reward that used to be created from nothing — level-ups (25k every level + a milestone of 250k × level/5 every 5th level), the welcome PAT, connect bonuses, redeem codes, chat raffles, top mic of the hour, mic challenge prizes, `!beg`, Pictionary, turf income and interest, the season prize match and the store heist: all come out of the Federal Reserve by default, and are **skipped when it can't cover them**. Turf upkeep, upgrades and claim/invasion buy-ins go to the Reserve. The **Vault flows & shortfall** table (under Automint) shows every PAT in and out of each vault by day and source, the daily shortfall, and a suggested automint. Prices and rewards that used to be hardcoded — heist buy-ins, showdown, turf claim/invasion, lotto ticket, bingo card, wager/market/loan fees, `!beg`/mic/Pictionary rewards — are rows in the Sink Rates card. **Automint** tops up a vault on a schedule (a daily amount, minted hourly) while it's below a target you set — the gap the economy can't fill on its own. **Shop Items** prices everything buyable plus the bonuses items carry (Bottle Service XP, burner heat reduction), and **Voice Store** handles per-voice pricing and royalties.
